description: MVP Phase - GitHub-integrated collaborative markdown editor with real-time editing, repository selection, folder navigation, and commenting system

introduction.overview: A real-time collaborative markdown editor that allows multiple users to edit documents simultaneously with seamless synchronization, similar to Google Docs or Microsoft Teams documents. The system is backed by GitHub for version control and storage, with automatic commits that are transparent to users. Users can also add review comments in sidebar threads to facilitate collaboration and feedback.

phases.PoC: Prove that real-time collaborative editing works with minimal features
phases.MVP: Production-ready version with authentication, GitHub integration, and comments

goals: Enable real-time collaborative editing of markdown documents with multiple concurrent users
Provide seamless GitHub integration with automatic background commits (no manual Git operations)
Implement sidebar comment threads for document reviews and discussions
Support basic markdown formatting (headings, bold, italic, lists, links)
Authenticate users securely via GitHub OAuth
Ensure conflict-free editing experience through Yjs CRDT real-time sync technology
nonGoals: Mobile native apps: Web-based only (responsive design acceptable)
Rich text (WYSIWYG) editor mode: Markdown source editing only
Real-time voice/video chat: Communication through comments only
Integrations with tools other than GitHub: No Notion, Confluence, or other platform syncs
AI-powered features: No auto-completion, grammar checking, or content generation
Spreadsheet/table editor: Tables rendered as markdown only, no Excel-like editing
Presentation mode: Focus on document editing, not slideshow creation

uiux: Clean, minimal interface: Focus on content, reduce UI clutter
Responsive design: Should work on desktop and tablet (mobile is non-goal but should degrade gracefully)
Split-pane editor: Markdown source on left, preview on right (or toggle view)
Sidebar for comments: Slides in from right, doesn't obstruct main editor
User avatars: Use GitHub profile pictures for authenticated users
Color coding: Each collaborator gets a distinct color for cursor and highlights
accessibility: Keyboard shortcuts for common formatting actions
Proper ARIA labels for screen readers

architecture.sessionStorage: Redis for user profiles and encrypted tokens

githubIntegration.repositoryStructure: Users can select any GitHub repository they have write access to
githubIntegration.commentStorage: Store comments as YAML files in GitHub under .mume/ folder
githubIntegration.commitStrategy: Batch changes from multiple users into single commits every 30-60 seconds to avoid excessive commit history
githubIntegration.authentication: GitHub OAuth with encrypted token storage

realTimeSync.conflictResolution: Yjs CRDT ensures character-level merging without conflicts
realTimeSync.networkResilience: Handle reconnection gracefully with exponential backoff, queue changes during disconnection

performance.documentSizeLimit: Start with reasonable limits (e.g., 1MB per document) to ensure real-time sync performance
performance.concurrentUsers: Support at least 10 concurrent users per document without degradation
performance.websocketPooling: Optimize server resources for many simultaneous documents
performance.caching: 5-minute TTL for repository lists and file trees

security.oauth: Validate OAuth tokens, use HTTPS only
security.tokenEncryption: AES-256-GCM encryption for stored GitHub tokens
security.rateLimiting: Prevent abuse of GitHub API and WebSocket connections
security.inputSanitization: Prevent XSS in markdown preview and comments

PoC.realTimeSync: Multiple users can edit simultaneously without merge conflicts
PoC.latency: Changes propagate to all users within 1 second
PoC.concurrentUsers: At least 3-5 users can edit the same document simultaneously
PoC.stability: PoC runs for 30+ minutes without crashes or data corruption

MVP.collaborationEffectiveness: Users can edit documents concurrently without experiencing merge conflicts or data loss
MVP.syncLatency: Changes propagate to all users within 1 second under normal network conditions
MVP.autoSaveReliability: 99.9% of edits successfully committed to GitHub without user intervention
MVP.userAdoption: Users prefer this tool over manual Git workflows for collaborative markdown editing
MVP.commentEngagement: At least 30% of documents have at least one comment thread (indicating review/collaboration usage)
MVP.documentAccessibility: Users can access any document from the GitHub repo within 2 seconds

successMetrics.Horizon1: To be defined based on feature set implemented

MVP.question: How do comments remain anchored when the document text changes around them?
MVP.recommendation: Use character offsets with Yjs position tracking for automatic updates

MVP.question: What's the upper limit of simultaneous editors per document?
MVP.recommendation: Start with 10-20 user limit for MVP, test and optimize in Horizon 1

openQuestions.Horizon1: To be defined when Horizon 1 planning begins

approach: Start with basic WebSocket server and simple name-based authentication
Integrate Yjs for CRDT (y-websocket for WebSocket provider, store document in memory with Y.Doc)
Add basic markdown preview (react-markdown, split-pane layout)
Implement cursor sharing (Yjs awareness API, assign random colors)
Test with multiple browser windows locally (3-5 tabs to simulate multi-user editing)
PoC.status: Completed - All PoC user stories implemented and passing

approach: Set up Redis with Docker Compose for session and user data
Implement GitHub OAuth and session management with encrypted token storage
Build GitHub service layer with Octokit for repository operations
Create repository selector and folder navigation UI
Implement automatic GitHub commits with conflict resolution
Build commenting system (YAML files in GitHub, sidebar UI, anchoring logic)
Add GitHub avatars to user presence indicators
MVP.status: Completed - All MVP user stories implemented and passing

userStories.title: Branch selection in document browser
userStories.description: As a user, I want to select a branch when browsing files so that I can view and edit documents from any branch, not just the default branch.
acceptanceCriteria: Branch selector dropdown added to DocumentBrowser page header, next to repository name
Branch selector fetches available branches via new backend endpoint: GET /api/repositories/:owner/:repo/branches
Default branch is pre-selected when first loading the document browser
Selecting a different branch reloads the file tree for that branch
URL updated to include branch: /repositories/:owner/:repo?branch=feature-xyz
Branch parameter passed to existing tree endpoint: GET /api/repositories/:owner/:repo/tree?branch=...
Backend GitHubService.getRepositoryTree() updated to accept optional branch parameter
New backend GitHubService.listBranches() method using octokit.rest.repos.listBranches()
Branch selection persists when navigating to editor and back to browser
Loading state shown while fetching branches and file tree
Error handling for branches that no longer exist (redirect to default branch with message)
Typecheck passes
Unit tests for branch listing and branch-specific tree fetching

userStories.title: Display branch in editor header breadcrumb
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see the repository name, current branch, and file path in the editor's top bar so that I always know which branch I'm editing on.
acceptanceCriteria: Editor breadcrumb updated to show: {owner}/{repo} > {branch} > {folder/path} > {filename}
Branch segment only displayed when NOT on the default branch (keep current behaviour for main)
Branch segment styled distinctly (e.g., with branch icon or different colour) to differentiate from folder path
Branch name truncated with ellipsis if too long (max ~20 characters with tooltip for full name)
Route updated to include branch: /repositories/:owner/:repo/edit/:branch/* (file path as wildcard)
Editor page extracts branch from URL and passes to document loading
Branch information passed to WebSocket document registration
Branch displayed in document browser header as well for consistency
Typecheck passes
Unit tests for breadcrumb rendering with and without branch display

userStories.title: Save to selected branch
userStories.description: As a user, I want my saves to commit to the branch I selected so that I can work on feature branches without affecting the main branch.
acceptanceCriteria: Branch parameter added to document registration: POST /api/repositories/:owner/:repo/register body includes branch
documentState.service.ts stores branch alongside other document metadata (SHA, token, dirty state)
GitHubService.updateFile() updated to accept branch parameter
octokit.rest.repos.createOrUpdateFileContents() call includes branch parameter
Auto-save job (githubSync.job.ts) commits to the stored branch for each document
Manual save endpoint commits to the document's registered branch
SHA tracking is branch-specific (different branches have different file SHAs)
Conflict resolution handles branch-specific conflicts
Save status indicator shows which branch was saved to (e.g., 'Saved to feature-branch')
Typecheck passes
Unit tests for branch-specific saving and SHA management

userStories.title: Create pull request from editor
userStories.description: As a user, I want to create a pull request from my current branch so that I can submit my changes for review without leaving the editor.
acceptanceCriteria: Create PR button added to editor header, visible when on a non-default branch
Button disabled with tooltip ('PRs can only be created from non-default branches') when on default branch
Clicking button opens CreatePRModal dialog component
Modal fetches and displays list of changed files via new endpoint: GET /api/repositories/:owner/:repo/compare/:baseBranch...:headBranch
Each file shown with checkbox (default: checked) to include/exclude from PR description
Files display change type indicator (added, modified, deleted)
Description field pre-filled with: 'Changes by {username} on {date}' (e.g., 'Changes by johndoe on 13 Jan 2026')
Description field is editable (textarea)
Title field added, pre-filled with branch name formatted as title (e.g., 'feature-new-login' becomes 'Feature new login')
PR always targets the repository's default branch (no target branch selector)
Create Pull Request button in modal calls: POST /api/repositories/:owner/:repo/pulls
Backend endpoint uses octokit.rest.pulls.create() to create PR
On success, user redirected to the PR URL on GitHub (opens in new tab)
Error handling for: no changes to compare, branch already has PR, API failures
Loading state while creating PR
Cancel button closes modal without action
Typecheck passes
Unit tests for modal component, file comparison, and PR creation endpoint
